source: PatWalters/rd_filters (MIT licensed), aggregating ChEMBL's structural_alerts table

PAINS.description: Substructures associated with frequent, non-specific hits across unrelated high-throughput screening assays -- via mechanisms like redox cycling, metal chelation, aggregation, or fluorescence/absorbance interference, not necessarily real biological activity or toxicity.
PAINS.citation: Baell, J. B.; Holloway, G. A. J. Med. Chem. 2010, 53 (7), 2719-2740.

Glaxo.description: Reactive, unstable, or otherwise undesirable functional groups from GlaxoWellcome's own compound-library triage rules (predating the 2000 merger that formed GlaxoSmithKline). Widely reused as a general-purpose reactive-group filter.

Dundee.description: A general-purpose set of reactive and undesirable functional groups, part of the same lineage of medicinal-chemistry structural filters commonly bundled with Glaxo/BMS/Inpharmatica in cheminformatics compound-quality pipelines (e.g. ChEMBL's own structural alerts).

BMS.description: Reactive and unstable functionality filters used in Bristol-Myers Squibb's internal compound triage -- covers a large number of specific reactive electrophiles, unstable heterocycles, and Michael acceptor variants.

SureChEMBL.description: Filters used by SureChEMBL (EMBL-EBI's patent-mining chemistry database, part of the ChEMBL family) to flag reactive or undesirable structures extracted from patent literature.

MLSMR.description: Filters used by the NIH Molecular Libraries Program to screen reactive, unstable, or promiscuous compounds out of its screening collection.

Inpharmatica.description: ADMET/compound-quality structural filters originally developed by Inpharmatica Ltd. (a UK cheminformatics company, later acquired by Galapagos), integrated into ChEMBL's own structural alerts.

LINT.description: A reactive/undesirable-functional-group filter set from Eli Lilly, distinct from the separate, more elaborate Lilly "Demerit" scoring system (Bruns & Watson 2012) -- this is a simpler SMARTS-pattern alert list, not the demerit-points rule engine.

patterns.title: R18 Quaternary C, Cl, I, P or S
